question: Define $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ by $f(1)=1$ and $f(n)=n-1$ for $n\geq2$. Examine whether $f$ is one-one and whether it is onto. Justify both conclusions.
explanation:
Testing the one-one property
We have
$$f(1)=1$$
and
$$f(2)=2-1=1.$$
Thus, $f(1)=f(2)$ although $1\ne2$. Therefore, $f$ is not one-one.

Testing the onto property
Let $y\in\mathbb{N}$. For $y=1$, we have $f(1)=1$. For $y>1$, choose $n=y+1$. Then $n\geq2$ and
$$f(y+1)=(y+1)-1=y.$$
Thus, every element of $\mathbb{N}$ has a pre-image.

Conclusion
The function $f$ is onto but not one-one.

options.B: $f$ is onto but not one-one because $f(1)=f(2)=1$
